title: Down Payments and Plan Availability under the Installment Payment Plans
content:
**1. The down payment.** On the **Installment Payment Plans**, the down payment is the premium portion — the full-term premium billed multiplied by the plan's new-business down payment percentage (for a new-business term) or its renewal down payment percentage (for a renewal term), divided by 100 and rounded to the cent — plus every fully earned fee charged with the term (the policy fee and any SR-22 or FR-44 filing fee), in full.

**2. Who may use an installment plan.** An installment plan is available only when the customer's count of returned payments in the rolling 12-month lookback does not exceed the plan's entry limit. A customer who exceeds it is offered only the Cardinal Point Paid-in-Full Plan.

| Plan | Entry limit: returned payments in 12 months | Recurring authorization needed before set-up |
|---|---|---|
| Cardinal Point Paid-in-Full Plan | no limit | none |
| Cardinal Point Two-Pay Plan | 1 | none |
| Cardinal Point Four-Pay Plan | 1 | none |
| Cardinal Point Six-Pay Direct Bill Plan | 1 | none |
| Cardinal Point Monthly EFT Plan | 1 | signed bank account (ACH) authorization |
| Cardinal Point Monthly Card Autopay Plan | 1 | signed debit or credit card authorization |

**3. Automatic draft plans.** A Monthly EFT or Monthly Card Autopay plan is set up only after the customer has signed a recurring payment authorization for it; the signed authorization on the plan's records is the evidence.

**4. Method.** A new-business down payment is accepted only by a down payment method of the plan (debit card, credit card, bank ACH, cash or money order on every plan).

**5. Outcome of the down payment.** When the down payment clears, the plan becomes current, or paid in full when the down payment was the whole premium. When the down payment is returned dishonored, the plan closes on that day, the returned-payment fee is charged, and the term is voided from inception under the policy's own rule.

**Worked example (hypothetical).** A new-business term on the Cardinal Point Six-Pay Direct Bill Plan with a full-term premium of 1,010.00, a policy fee of 25.00 and an SR-22 filing fee of 15.00 has a premium portion of 20 percent of 1,010.00, which is 202.00, and a down payment of 202.00 plus 25.00 plus 15.00, which is 242.00. A customer with two returned payments in the last 12 months exceeds the entry limit of 1 and is offered only the Cardinal Point Paid-in-Full Plan.

The returned-payment count is read from the system's ledger across all of the customer's plans; the percentages per plan are those of the plan schedule.
